Compensation: Is salary guaranteed and for how long?
Is there productivity, panel, quality, call, newborn-rounding, or patient-access bonus?
What is the wRVU or encounter expectation at full ramp?
Are phone call, weekend clinic, newborn nursery, or hospital rounding paid separately?
How are no-shows, vaccine visits, nurse visits, forms, and portal work handled in productivity?
Are sign-on, relocation, CME, board fees, licensing, and loan repayment available?
Clinical model: What is expected visits/day at full ramp?
What is the schedule template for well checks, sick visits, newborns, ADHD, behavioral health, and complex care?
How many rooms, MAs, nurses, and front-desk staff per physician?
Who handles forms, prior authorizations, refill requests, portal messages, and school/camp paperwork?
Is newborn nursery rounding required, optional, or compensated separately?
Are lactation, behavioral health, care management, interpreters, and vaccine support available?
What is the payer mix and Medicaid percentage?
APP supervision: Will NPs/PAs report to or collaborate with me?
How many APPs would I supervise?
Is supervision compensated by stipend, RVU credit, percentage of collections, chart-review fee, or not at all?
Who signs charts, handles escalations, covers inbox, and manages liability?
Are APP visits counted toward my panel access or productivity expectations?
Quality bonus: What metrics drive quality bonus: vaccines, well-child rates, access, HEDIS, asthma care, depression screening, patient experience, or portal response time?
What is the maximum quality bonus and historical average payout?
Are targets adjusted for patient population, Medicaid mix, staffing shortages, and no-show rates?
Are quality metrics individual, clinic-wide, or system-wide?
Lifestyle / call: How often is phone call? Is nurse triage first-line?
Are nights, weekends, holidays, and newborn rounding required before clinic?
Is there flexibility for part-time, 4-day week, or school pickup hours?
How much inbox work remains after hours?
Contract risk: What is the noncompete and does it restrict outpatient pediatrics broadly?
Is malpractice occurrence or claims-made, and who pays tail?
What happens to panel ownership if I leave?

Clinical Fit: Schedule template supports safe well/sick/behavioral/complex care.
Staffing handles vaccines, forms, triage, prior auths, and portal messages.
Compensation Upside: Call, newborns, panel growth, quality bonus, and productivity are transparent.
Lifestyle Fit: Phone call, weekend clinic, nursery rounding, and after-hours inbox are manageable.
Risk Safety: Noncompete, tail, panel ownership, and unilateral productivity changes are clear.
Strategic Fit: Clinic location, patient panel, and system reputation help long-term practice growth.
Collaborative Fit: Nurses, behavioral health, lactation, care managers, APPs, and specialists are accessible.
